speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your delayed menarche and unusual physical features, have you experienced any frequent fractures or bone pain in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's history of partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly, severe acne, and fractures despite minor trauma is highly suggestive of a disorder of sexual development. Given the maternal history of hirsutism during pregnancy, I need to know if you have been told you have ambiguous genitalia or if you were assigned male at birth.

REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, karyotype, and pelvic ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: 17-hydroxyprogesterone: Elevated; Karyotype: 46,XY; Pelvic Ultrasound: Normal male internal genitalia (absent uterus, normal prostate and seminal vesicles).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently taking oral isotretinoin for acne and an oral contraceptive. Social history: The patient is a high school student without significant tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any recent illnesses, appetite change, or weight change. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The patient's history of ambiguous genitalia at birth (labial fusion, clitoromegaly), maternal hirsutism, severe acne, and bone fragility is classic for this condition, not Tuberculosis as the previous note suggested. I have already ordered the necessary hormonal and genetic tests to confirm this.
